answer: Every fake identity, or knoll, must anchor its public key inside the karst, a global hardware registry tracking physical secure enclaves by factory root certificate. Enrolling a knoll consumes cedar, defined as exclusive host-attestation proofs that increase in price per head because the karst charges an exponentially rising stake in ETH for every additional agent bound to the same hardware manufacturer batch. Because clones from the same server farm collide at the karst batch counter, the marginal bill in ETH doubles per new knoll, failing only if a chipmaker is bribed to forge root keys.
